comments.text: Too expensive here for me unfortunately, where do you get yours from?
comments.author: @PolarIceCreamery

comments.text:
​ @PolarIceCreamery I got my first batch from Hoosier Farms, then that became unavailable here in sweden, then I just bought from a place in France called labo and gato. I paid 43 euros for 1 kilo, I use 1:2 water reconstitution ratio, about 6g of powder to one yolk (17g total) so I get 160 ish yolks out of a kilo. That breaks down to 30 cents (us) or 40 cents(  Canadian) per yolk, and I don't have the hassle of farting about with fresh eggs ( the convenience and price wins over fresh for now) or chucking the white, I don't like to waste either.

 I'm trying to perfect my keto ice cream, and I'm getting pretty close now, I'm adjusting the yolk powder batch by batch. Previous batch had too much, so not enough overrun, a bit harder scoopability but zero icyness. Most recent batch had great scoopability but a touch of icyness. I'm excited about the next batch!  If you're interested I can make a video about it, I'd love your input. I'm just a happy amateur of course, but I'm having a lot of fun😊

I use eye droppers that have ml increments marked on the side for all extracts and emulsions I add to my ice creams. I add five ml to a mix, stir and taste. If more is needed, I add five ml at a time, tasting as I go. As you get closer to your desired taste add fewer ml at a time until you get it just right.

Note: keep records of how much flavoring you add, and keep your batch sizes consistent.
